problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to \,-1}[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+t \\ {e}^{t+1} \\ \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)}{t}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) \\ 2 \\ \frac{1-2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}({t}^{2}+t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}{e}^{t+1} \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)}{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}+(-1) \\ {e}^{-1+1} \\ \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-1+1)}{(-1)}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}2 \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}\frac{1-2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1+1) \\ 2 \\ \frac{1-2(-1)}{(-1)^{2}+1})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =0(0)+1(2)+(-1)(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
